title: Characterizing the CLS Token Bottleneck Failure in Vision SAEs

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with a gap: showing that CLS token SAE features become less interpretable at classification-relevant layers is informative but the path to a safety intervention is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses pre-trained ViT-Prisma SAEs (no training needed). Requires computing sparsity, coherence, and class-specificity metrics across layers and token types. Intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three metrics across three layer groups and two token types (CLS vs. spatial). Sustained effort but well-structured. Feasible in 30 hours with guidance.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple recent works have documented the CLS token vs. spatial token divergence in vision SAEs, including sparsity differences, class-token feature frequency by layer, and the compositional nature of CLS features in deep layers. The specific 'bottleneck failure' framing and systematic three-metric characterization adds modest novelty, but the core observations are already established.

evidence.source: Steering CLIP's Vision Transformer with Sparse Autoencoders (arXiv 2504.08729, 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies SAE features in CLIP ViTs and documents differences in CLS vs spatial token activation patterns, including L0 sparsity differences across token types.

evidence.source: Causal Interpretation of Sparse Autoencoder Features in Vision (arXiv 2509.00749, 2025)
evidence.finding: Investigates causal roles of SAE features in vision transformers, documenting how class-token features encode compositional concepts in deeper layers.
Open-source toolkit documenting extreme L0 differences between CLS and spatial tokens (L0 of 122,631 per CLS token), and class-token feature frequency rising sharply in higher layers.
